protocolNote: quiesce-scan keeps protocol 1 when the other holder-lock routes moved to 2 (2026-10-20): its callers (the cutover fence, fgctl activation) pin it separately and it is read-only, so a stale payload gains nothing by being refused here
description: Read-only scan that tells a cutover whether any other fgOS process of the given workspace is still running. It finds that workspace's writers only; stopping every writer on every machine is the operator's procedure. It never signals or modifies anything.

optional.meaning: workspace root (main checkout) to scan for; at least one required
a linked worktree of the single --root, as the caller's Git listing names it; with more than one --root it is a usage error
pids that are not counted (the caller and its own ancestors)

linux: /proc/*/cwd inside the root or inside any --dir the caller listed, counted only when the process could be fgOS (node, bun, deno, fgos, fgos-runner, fgos-gateway, or an argv that cannot be read), so an idle shell or agent session is not a writer; with --workspace-only every such cwd counts and the caller filters; the route never runs Git

/proc/*/cmdline carrying a typed --dir, --worktree or --cwd value (or the value after -C) that resolves inside the root or a listed --dir, relative values resolved at the process's cwd, with the same could-be-fgOS rule. No other argument counts: a prompt or positional path is text, and a fgOS binary name, a release path or a pinned FGOS_STATE_ROOT of another workspace never counts
scan.otherPlatforms: result unavailable: a person confirms that no fgOS process is left
scan.unreadableEntries: an entry of the caller's own uid that cannot be read (permission, vanished) is counted in unreadable, never treated as clean, unless its readable argv rules it out: argv[0] names neither node (node, nodejs, node<version>), bun, deno nor a fgOS binary (fgos, fgos-runner, fgos-gateway); an unreadable argv always counts

processes.cmdline: string (argv joined by spaces, for people)

exitCodes.10: processes: at least one process found, or unreadable > 0

invariants: clean is only returned when unreadable == 0
the scan runs before and after the fences are placed; the caller refuses to continue on any result other than clean
